key_insight: 2D/3D perovskite interfaces can strongly reshape work function, macroscopic potential, and band alignment, with the exact effect depending on surface cleavage, termination, and chemical composition.
engineering_relevance: Interface chemistry in passivated perovskite solar cells must be controlled precisely because it can shift valence and conduction offsets enough to affect carrier extraction and device stability.
method: Hybrid functional calculations for structural/electronic properties
Work function, electron affinity, and band offset analysis across 2D/3D interfaces
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary hybrid-functional results showing work-function dependence on surface chemistry and band offsets spanning roughly 0.2 to 0.7 eV.
watch_item: Results are preliminary and highly surface- and termination-dependent, so conclusions may not directly generalize across all perovskite stacks or real device conditions.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
